Happy new year to you all… For me, The end of the year always helps to put things into perspective. Growth doesn’t really happen unless you’re willing to challenge yourself physically, mentally, and emotionally. That’s something I try to live by and keep coming back to as I learn more with each passing year. 

I’m so grateful for my loving and supportive family and for meaningful career with people I care deeply about and for all the time spent showing up for both. And throw in a lot of laughs, long energetic walks, and way too much fun with the dogs. And for family moments big and small that actually matter more than anything else.

For me it’s never about chasing perfection... Just a lot of memories, a lot of lessons, and a reminder to keep reflecting, keep improving, and keep choosing the harder, better path forward! Because true growth only happens outside your comfort zone… And when you surround yourself with people that inspire you to dig deeper and reach farther than you thought, you’ll be amazed at how far you can go… I wish everyone a healthy, happy blessed new year and may 2026 be your best year yet❤️❤️❤️

What a special thanksgiving weekend with the people I love most! Laughing, playing, eating too much… and enjoying our family and football and tradition in the state of Michigan. I am so blessed to work with the best team at @foxsports delivering a great game between the Lions and the Packers.

Working with Kevin Burkhardt and Erin Andrews and Tom Rinaldi and Dean Blandino and our entire crew made last Thursday so much fun. And then to travel shortly down the road to Ann Arbor to watch the most athletic Brady family member to ever play at Michigan, my niece Hannah, who plays for the Wolverines Volleyball team, and spend time with all of my extended family made this one of the best Thanksgivings ever.

It’s always such a special experience being on the Michigan campus, especially now that I don’t have to take finals anymore! 😜 We got to go to the big house to see Michigan football take on a great Ohio State team 😡 And to see so many former teammates and friends meant the
world to me. I’m so appreciative and grateful for all the incredible memories and relationships that have been created since I started at Michigan in 1995.

And to share that experience and all those memories with my kids was a dream come true. The game didn’t quite turn out the way we hoped (I still maintain it was a touchback!🤣) But the sun always comes up the next day, and to realize that it was one of the best weekends of my life, surrounded by the love of my parents, meant the world to me. I look forward to coming back soon and to finishing the NFL season strong and creating more unforgettable memories with this crew. Sending my love and gratitude to you all and I hope you had an incredible Thanksgiving as well. Even the people in Columbus 😉

Opening the 5th CardVault by Tom Brady yesterday was special, and not just because of the turnout. It reminded me why I fell in love with collecting in the first place. This hobby brings people together. Kids, parents, lifelong fans, all connecting over shared memories, favorite players, and the stories behind the cards.

There’s something powerful about walking into a space where generations can bond over their favorite teams, where a kid’s first pack might spark a lifelong passion, and where the history of sports comes alive in your hands. That’s what we’re building with CardVault, not just stores, but homes for the hobby and the spaces around it.

Huge thank you to the entire CardVault team, our incredible partners, the passionate collectors, and the East Hampton community for welcoming us with open arms. You made it a day we’ll never forget. Grateful to be a part of this movement, and even more excited for what’s ahead.

What a special night opening the doors to @cardvaultbytombrady at American Dream Mall in New Jersey. This is more than just a store — it’s a dream come full circle. When I was a kid in San Mateo, I’d spend hours at my local card shop, what’s on second, flipping through cards, trading with friends, and falling in love with the hobby. That joy shaped so much of my love for sports. And seeing so many fans and friends last night brought so much happiness to what already is a very exciting time. Thank you to everyone who works so hard the past six weeks to make this happen and over the past many years to bring card vault by Tom Brady to life. We have a great team, and we’re just getting started.

With CardVault, our goal is to bring that same excitement to a new generation of collectors— making card collecting fun, accessible, and something kids (and kids at heart) can share together. More locations, across the country and across the world, are coming soon. 

PS: I’m still recovering from seeing all those cheering Giants and Jets fans, usually someone is trying to kill me, or something terrible happens when I’m around you guys 😂😂😂

Turn on the television any time of day, and there’s a good chance you’ll see the welcoming, gap-toothed grin of Michael Strahan. The former New York Giants defensive end is a co-host of Good Morning America, and on weekends sits along other NFL greats as a football analyst and commentator for Fox NFL Sunday. Early this spring, he also reprised his game show hosting role on ABC’s eighth season of The $100,000 Pyramid.⁠
⁠
It’s a diverse career that keeps him on his toes, and Strahan says that’s exactly how he likes it. “It’s exciting because everything I do is unique,” says Strahan. “Hosting a game show is nothing like doing an NFL show, which is nothing like doing GMA and the news. They all make me exercise a completely different part of my brain.”⁠
⁠
This mental fitness in his 50s is a healthy complement to the physical fitness Strahan, a professional athlete for 15 years, long had as his focus. These days, wellness means a more balanced mind/body approach. Read the full interview with Michael Strahan by tapping the link in the @WebMD bio.

STILL ON TOP
31 Years and Counting as the #1 NFL Pregame Show.
Photographed by @johnrussophoto
C U R T   M E N E F E E 
JR} Who inspired you to be in your chosen profession of a broadcaster?
CM} I never dreamed of being on television. It wasn’t in my world of reality at all. But I was a huge fan of local broadcasters growing up in Atlanta.  Listening to Ernie Johnson, Sr. or Skip Carey on a Braves game was magical. 

T E R R Y   B R A D S H A W 
JR} What is the most memorable moment of your career and why?
TB} My most memorable moment of my career was winning Super Bowl IX.  We defeated the Minnesota Vikings 16-6 in Tulane Stadium in New Orleans.  Not only was it my first Super Bowl win, but it was the first for our beloved owner, Art Rooney, Sr.

H O W I E   L O N G 
JR} What was the biggest challenge you had to overcome during your career?  How did you manage it?
HL} My biggest challenge I had to overcome during my career was injuries, playing injured and subsequent surgeries.  Then the coming back over and over again.  

M I C H A E L   S T R A H A N 
JR} What changes do you foresee in the NFL’s future and what would you like to see happen?
MS} I’m not sure what changes will come in the future of the NFL, but I would like to see the game continue to protect the players.  The biggest thing for me is keeping it competitive and entertaining.

J I M M Y   J O H N S O N 
JR} What was the biggest challenge you had to overcome during your career? 
JJ} My most difficult time was going 1-15 in my first year as head coach of the Dallas Cowboys.

R O B   G R O N K O W S K I
JR} What advice would you give younger aspiring NFL players?
RG} I would tell young athletes that aspire to reach the NFL to first make sure you are on the right path with your journey. You must love the game of football to make it to the top. 

J A Y   G L A Z E R 
JR} What was the biggest challenge you had to overcome during your career?  How did you manage it?
JG} It took me eleven years to get my first full time job.  It was BRUTAL!  Getting rejected for eleven years because I didn’t do the job like everyone else took a lot from my soul.

Family bonds
Resilance - I would love to hear your stories on how you were able to stay resilient in a situation.

At my last US Open, a good friend of mine JR Ridinger posted his last ever post here on IG. Of course at the time none of us knew that it would be his last - but it was about me and how proud he was of me in my final tournament. He had stayed up to watch me win a great battle. The next day, I got news that he had passed due to a blood clot. This was super triggering to me because I myself almost died of the same thing. Only because it was caught in time. What made me so fortunate and not others? I was flooded with emotions and all the moments we spent together with his wife one of my best friends, Loren Ridinger. 

How do we move forward? How do we keep going? It was a devastating setback. In this amazing book, Loren discovers how to continue to live your best life after losing your greatest love. It's something she still deals with today, but we know that JR would be so proud of her. Congrats @lorenridinger. This is indeed a MUST READ.

World Champion gymnast and longtime Friends of the Children ambassador @simonebiles visited @friendschicago to share her story, spend time with youth, and answer their questions.

One of our favorite moments was when Vanessa* asked, "Do you ever say anything negative about yourself and how do you stop?" Simone replied, "Sometimes you think you're too short or you're too tall... you're perfect just how you are and so I try to do my affirmations every single day." 

Then Simone led our youth through some of her favorite affirmations including, "I am brave", "I am loved", and "I am important".

Simone deeply connects with the mission of Friends of the Children and the youth we serve. Simone is an inspiration to our youth, showing them what is possible when they work hard to achieve their goals and have a team of support by their side. 

Thank you, Simone, for showing up for our youth and for your continued support, leadership, and belief in the power of individualized and intentional Professional Mentorship. For 12+ years, no matter what.

As a mom of two, @alexmorgan13 is approaching feeding — and motherhood in general —differently.

No more comparisons. No more pressure. No more outside noise. Just doing what works best for her and her family.

For Alex, that means turning to Bobbie to help nourish her son, Enzo, when they need it.
“As a mom, there will always be comparisons… but I don’t feel pressure from the outside noise to do things a certain way. My journey with my son is mine and my husband’s — and ours only.” - Alex Morgan

Bobbie is proud to partner with 2x World Champion and 2x Bobbie Mom Alex Morgan to remind parents that there’s no scoreboard in motherhood, and we’re proud to be her infant formula of choice. 💚

There’s no scoreboard in motherhood.

As a mom of two about to retire her jersey, “winning” looks different from what it used to for 2x World Champion soccer icon @alexmorgan13. On the field, it was about competition. She’s teamed up with Bobbie, as the newest member of their MotherBoard, to not only support her combo feeding journey but to support a shared mission in motherhood: confidence over comparison.

Sometimes, it feels like early parenthood comes with an unwritten playbook—track the sleep, track the ounces, measure the milestones, feed the “right” way. But motherhood isn’t about outperforming anyone (not even yourself). It’s about showing up, trusting your gut, and cheering each other on.

Because when every mom feels like she’s losing, there are no victories. But when we start honoring the moments that matter most, that’s how we change the game.

The Art Arena Podcast, hosted by acclaimed broadcaster Cari Champion, is a celebration of stories that live at the crossroads of sport and culture, aiming to bridge creative, athletic, and diverse communities through candid conversations with talent who defy categorization.

This was the live recording of the first episode of The Art Arena Podcast, which took place at the Art Arena Summit at The Rockaway Hotel, where sports broadcaster and journalist Cari Champion explores the dynamic intersection of creativity and athleticism. In this conversation, Cari sits down with two-time World Champion, Olympic Gold Medalist, and activist Megan Rapinoe to unpack the power of creative expression on and off the field.

Together, they dive into what drives creativity—in sport, in life, and in culture—discussing how athletes channel passion, individuality, and purpose into projects off the pitch. From bold fashion statements to social impact initiatives, this episode highlights how the worlds of art and athletics are deeply connected through collaboration, identity, and inspiration. At the link in bio, discover the full conversation on our YouTube channel and wherever you get your podcasts.

“Pressure is survival. Basketball is a privilege.”
That was Phillip “Sarge” Harrison — the Army drill sergeant who raised Shaquille O’Neal @shaq and built one of the most dominant forces the NBA has ever seen.
Before Game 4 of the 2002 NBA Finals, in Shaq’s hometown of New Jersey, Sarge reminded him what he was trained to do: finish the mission. Discipline. Accountability. No excuses. Never repeat the same mistake twice.
Shaq responded the only way he knew how.
Game 4: 34 PTS | 10 REB | 4 AST | 2 BLK | 60% FG
Finals averages: 36.3 PPG | 12.3 RPG | 2.8 BPG
A 113–107 win, a series sweep, and Shaq’s third straight Finals MVP.

You know the feeling when you're trying to squeeze into a tight spot and everyone around you is screaming "it's not gonna work"? But you're determined to prove them wrong. You start to bend, to twist, to contort yourself into impossible shapes, all in the name of making it fit.

But let's be real, sometimes it's just not meant to be. The walls are too narrow, the space is too small, and no matter how hard you try, you just can't seem to make it work. The voices of doubt start to creep in, "we need a bigger car", "this ain't gonna work", and before you know it, you're ready to throw in the towel.

But what if you didn't give up? What if you kept pushing, kept trying, and kept believing that you could make it work? Maybe, just maybe, you'd be surprised at what you can achieve. So the next time you're faced with an impossible task, remember: it's not about the size of the space, it's about the size of your determination. Will you make it work, or will you give up and walk away? The choice is yours.

How I’m leaving 2025

He was 7’3”. He had NBA interest. And he still chose a different path. Jordan Wilmore walked away from basketball dreams because he wanted something bigger than a contract… he wanted to serve.

Jordan finished the police academy, passed everything in front of him, and then hit the final hurdle. He failed the state exam by one single point. That one point meant working a second job, stretching himself thin, and possibly watching the dream slip away.

Then Shaq heard the story. Three words: “I got you.” Shaq stepped in to cover Jordan’s living expenses so he could focus fully on earning that last point. No distractions. No second job. Just belief, support, and a reminder that the right people always show up at the right time.

Sometimes the real wins don’t come on a scoreboard. Sometimes they come from choosing purpose… and having someone make sure you get the chance to finish what you started.

Only ICON was on hand as Russell Wilson (@dangerusswilson) got ready for his first-ever Met Gala — joining Ciara (@ciara) on fashion’s biggest night. The NY Giants quarterback suited up in a custom FRÈRE (@frere) look, crafted by the Black-owned luxury label known for sharp tailoring and elevated silhouettes. “The black tiger stripe along the pattern of the jacket really represents both culture and elegance,” he explained, referencing this year’s theme. “This is about Black legacy… about the tradition of Black men and women using fashion for self-expression.”

Of course the moment wasn’t just about fashion. “I get to go with the prettiest lady on the Western and Eastern hemisphere,” he beamed.

Tony Hawk on Fast Times at Ridgemont High - the film he’s been watching, quoting and living with since 1982.

Before skateboarding was cool. Before anyone knew his name. Before the future made sense. From VHS rewatches and Spicoli impressions to meeting Sean Penn years later and finally settling the ‘buds vs buzz’ debate, this is a love letter to a film that felt real.

A time capsule of teenage life, punk-adjacent taste, skate culture on the margins and the feeling of knowing you’re different before you know where that difference will take you.

I was on a 1984 TV show in Japan about kids with talent. The direct translation of the show name is “Kids Great Assembly.” Each kid had to be under 16 so the asked me to lie about my age (since I had just turned 16). They also asked me to change the name of tricks - except Judo and Japan airs - because they “don’t translate well.” I used a section of the plexiglass halfpipe (a literal half-pipe) to jump the reluctant audience volunteers in the studio segment. Watching this back it all feels like an SnL skit or a bad fever dream… or maybe one big Varial American Dream. There is no info about this particular show online, so I’m still not sure if it actually happened. 
Thanks to @don_brown for sharing the original broadcast and to @bail.gun.gary for sending me this 9:16 edit.

I don’t know the exact criteria for Thrasher’s Skater Of The Year but here is my take for 2025: while we have seen some of the most incredible and inspiring street performances over the last year, Tom Schaar has single-handedly raised the profile and possibilities of vertical skateboarding. His skating is masterful and creative, on a level not seen since Danny & Bob enlightened us with what it means to truly go big (earning each of them well-deserved SOTY titles). And Tom somehow does it all with a style that is simultaneously stoic and fluid. His skating is now inspiring people to ride ramps and bowls for the first time - on a global scale - flipping the script on what a “vert button” actually is (in his case, it represents “replay” instead of “fast-forward). And here he is - less than a week after dropping a revolutionary part - pushing the limits of possibilities above Bob’s 28-foot monster quarter. The Tom Train has left the station at mega-speed and looks to be unstoppable, making him our obvious choice for 2025 SOTY
🎥: @tweestopher

1980 Gold Cup amateur finals at Marina Del Rey keyhole: this was my second competition as a sponsored skater and it was very intimidating. But I managed to keep this last run together, including a few of my own trick creations (body varial rock, bs varial & 1/2 cab to fs rock) even though I ran out of time from lack of speed. The most memorable part of this whole event happened as I was leaving; I saw @eddieelguera trying to learn my last trick - a variation of his own frontside rock - in the small (brown) bowl near the entrance of the park. It was the first time another skater seemed interested in what I had to offer (and I considered him among the best at the time). Seeing him emulating my move was much more validating than any trophy. 
I love everything about this clip: the era, the pool, the colors, the music and the fire we all had for something that nobody else cared about.

Back in the early ‘80s sponsored skaters were expected to compete in all events for overall points: pool (vert), freestyle, slalom, banked slalom and this: pipe pasting. You put a sticker in your hand and place it as high as possible. Most people went frontside for obvious reasons but I was always more consistent going backside, since you had to make it back down or it didn’t count. Not that it mattered; I never placed that well. The first couple of “pro grade” skateboards I had were blank decks that my dad bought at the Spring Valley swap meet. I used to put stickers on them and tell people they were prototype shapes from whichever company gave me the stickers. So I probably claimed this one was a Variflex. To add further confusion, I put a Bones sticker on it even though I was riding Sims Snakes. Anything to distract from my dorky style. Other notable details: volleyball pads, Norcon helmet, Dolphin (?) shorts, and possibly my first “wheeler” at the end of the Oasis snake run. This is 1978 on full display. At least I passed the sock check.

In early 2005, I was approached by Activision (via Tim Riley) about a standalone soundtrack release to THAW that would include current bands covering classic punk songs. It was an exciting idea, but I worried that the original artists might not agree to their songs being reimagined. The immediate response was mostly positive, including ones I thought would be reluctant (like Minor Threat, Bad Brains & Fear) and the covers that got recorded soon after were inspired. The album became such a success that I ended up doing several interviews & appearances based only on the 14-track CD (in addition to the usual press surrounding a game release). My favorite track from this project was Alkaline Trio choosing the TSOL deep cut Wash Away. But the best accolade (?) was getting an email from Paul Simonon asking if I would send signed skateboards to his sons in exchange for appropriating his London Calling cover shot.

My skating has been challenged lately in a way that is unfamiliar. Most injuries, aches and pains over my career have been temporary and/ or manageable, but this malady has staying power. I am proactively trying to remedy - or hold back the tide of - something potentially degenerative and it’s been a lot of work. I am lucky and thankful to have so many available resources in the form of experts, supplements, treatments and steely discipline (aka stubbornness). So for now, here is the skate of things: less speed, fewer airs and minimal twisting, relegated to mostly lip tricks; staying on my grind in the most literal sense. And still worth it.

“Seeing what I was able to do in the game really inspired me to pick up a board for the first time in my life and just start skating. I figured if I could manual in the game for 20 minutes straight while doing multiple handstands, then hitting a 900 in real life should be no problem. I was right," said Hawk.

Tony first asked me to be in his game (THPS II) in what seemed an afterthought after meeting for lunch when I busted my ankle ~1999. All I needed was advice from a Friend, yet he left me with a bigger gift than I could’ve ever asked for. At first, the Honor of Tony bringing me into that crazy circle of skaters was the coolest part, yet over time, it’s the friendships that’ve meant the most, including those with Lisa Hudson, Joel, Ralph plus the wizards who made the game so special. Now, after 25 years, Activision remastered THPS 3+4, adding new levels, music, and more. Check it out if you get the time. Most of all: Thank you Tony for all you’ve done and do for us!

I can’t believe I’ve arrived in Milan to represent my country at the Olympic Games for the third time. If you told little me that, she wouldn’t believe you
This one feels especially meaningful for so many reasons.

My parents left South Korea in search of a better future for their family. They left behind everything they knew so that my sisters and I could have the chance to one day live the American dream. Their sacrifice is one I will never take for granted.

So when I stand at the top of the halfpipe, competing on the biggest stage in sport, I do so with immense pride. I am representing my country but I am also representing those who took a leap of faith, who came to this beautiful nation carrying hopes, dreams, and courage.

I am proud of my heritage.
I am proud of my journey.
And I am proud to represent a country that is strongest when it embraces diversity, dignity, and hope.

For Olympic gold medalist @chloekim, her rise to fame was a double edged sword.

After she won her first X Games gold at 14,  Kim says she received “very racist, very hateful” comments online. “It made me feel so terrible,” she says. “As a young girl, that’s incredibly detrimental to my body image, my identity, everything … I had never experienced hate in that way.” The more she won, the worse the comments got. By 16, she says, “I was winning everything, and I felt like people wanted to take away from my talent and my hard work, and not give me the credit I deserved. I was foolish enough to believe them, too.” It took a long time for her to heal. “Now I don’t care,” she says. “Say what you want.”

Kim hopes other Asian American girls following in her footsteps will have a better experience, like 19-year-old Olympic hopeful Bea Kim. “I’m glad that I had to deal with that so she doesn’t have to, or doesn’t have to experience it to the extent that I have. And I hope she can carry on in her career with all the confidence, and do even greater things than me,” she tells ELLE.

Two-time Olympic gold medalist @chloekim is a beast in competition. 

She zigzags down the course, soaring about a dozen feet in the air, creating magic. “Chloe’s got several tricks that only one or two other athletes are doing,” her coach of over 10 years, Rick Bower, tells ELLE. As she attempts to secure her third Olympic gold at this year’s Winter Games, it’s clear Kim is the “woman to beat out there.” At this year’s games, she’ll first be competing in the women’s halfpipe qualifications before advancing to the finals, where she’ll have three runs to earn gold. “That’s less than two minutes total,” Kim notes. It’s clear she’s got her work cut out for her, but there’s nothing stopping her from going for the gold—not even a recent shoulder injury. 

In ELLE’s February 2026 digital cover story speaks to Kim about her potential history-making gold medal win, the toll training takes on her mental health, and her aspirations outside of Olympic glory. Read the full interview at the link in bio.

After winning her second Olympic gold medal in 2022, @chloekim almost walked away from the sport entirely. Now, the legendary snowboarder is back—and ready to make history.

Tied with @shaunwhite for the most X Games superpipe gold medals, Kim continues to push the boundaries of her sport—and the laws of physics. Still, after all her victories, Kim believes “my biggest accomplishment is always being able to get back up and try again.” 

This month, the world will watch her try again for Olympic gold at the 2026 Winter Games. If she wins, she’ll become the first person ever to win three back-to-back snow-board halfpipe gold medals. As the number-one-ranked female halfpipe snowboarder in the world, she clinched a spot on Team USA back in April. But despite all the noise and pressure to perform, Kim’s main focus is herself: “I’m just trying to be as happy as possible, whatever that looks like.”

In ELLE’s February 2026 digital cover story, Kim tells @ericagonzo about the racism she experienced after winning her first gold medal, reflects on her rise to stardom as a young athlete, and the heights she’s yet to reach. Read the full interview at the link in bio.

2012: Usain Bolt’s Golden Double

On August 9, 2012, Jamaican sprint superstar Usain Bolt secured his historic “golden double” at the 2012 London Olympics by winning the men’s 200-meter dash in 19.32 seconds. This victory made him the first man in history to win both the 100-meter and 200-meter Olympic sprint titles consecutively at the Olympic Games. He had previously won both events at the 2008 Beijing Olympics.

This isn’t a surfing conversation. It’s a conversation about longevity, alignment, and staying passionate in a world designed to disconnect you. You guys have got to check this one out.

I had a recent bodyscan done at @prenuvo to get a rundown of all the potential health concerns I know about and want to check in on or am unaware of and need to address now that I’m off tour and have some downtime. As you can read, I had a few minor and moderate findings to address which I won’t go over here. Clearly my scoliosis, which I’ve spoken about many times, is a serious issue but there were a few things I was unaware of that I reviewed with their doctor to either deal with or keep in mind as I continue future scans and see any noticeable changes. Showing my spine feels super personal as it’s crazy to see the curvature I’ve dealt with all these years but I think it’s important people know we all deal with physical ailments and can find ways to minimize their impacts and potentially reverse what comes up. These scans are especially important for people in their 50’s and beyond and I’m super thankful Prenuvo were able to find me a time in the short window I had to make it into their clinic. Only issue for me was I re-injured my hip a couple days after this and wish I had gotten the imagery to see any new damage there. We’ll review that next time. 🙏🏽 prenuvo.com/KELLYSLATER for $300 off scans. Link will be in story. I was also informed I’m supposed to say this is an #ad. I got a free scan but no payment. Welcome to WME, @kellyslater! ——— Over his 30+ year career, Kelly Slater has changed the landscape of surfing. He holds nearly every major record in the sport. With 11 World Surf League (WSL) titles and 56 WSL career victories, Kelly has the distinction of being both the youngest and oldest person to ever win a world title.

Beyond surfing, Kelly has built a global platform around sustainability and wellness. In 2014, he founded @outerknown, a sustainable clothing brand committed to responsible production practices. He also acquired majority ownership of Firewire Surfboards—considered the most sustainable surfboard platform in the world—and later launched Slater Designs. In 2015, he introduced the Kelly Slater Wave Company, creators of the world’s most advanced wave technology.
 
Kelly has appeared in Baywatch, Surf’s Up, The Ultimate Surfer, Momentum Generation, Ballers, Carpool Karaoke, Make or Break, and more. He presented at the 94th Academy Awards and was the focus of the 2024 portrait book A Life of Waves. He is also the author of two bestselling books and was featured in the Activision video game Kelly Slater Pro Surfer.

Shane Herring. He best blended the old school power and pure lines with the new school mentality and speed in the 90’s. In the years we spent traveling and surfing together, I always found Shane to be a kindhearted guy and an extremely talented surfer, but he had his demons that limited his time of greatness. He made a bigger mark than he might be known for these days and it hurts to know we won’t get to catch up again. I was really looking forward to seeing and maybe even surfing again in the coming months with Shane, whom I haven’t seen in probably 20+ years. waking up and starting to realize it was indeed not a dream. 

losing in the finals here 3 years ago had created a lot of doubt in my head. I thought I could never overcome the pressure, I thought holding this trophy would never happen. I  thought my dreams were so close to happening but would never come true. So to be here…. means absolutely everything. The more I started to dig deeper into my thoughts, I realized deep down I  didn’t truly believe any of those thoughts, deep down I realized that I can do it and I refused to let those thoughts consume me. the younger coco would have looked at me crazy because that girl never doubted a thing in her life especially when it came to tennis. But needless to say, I learned having doubt enter your head is impossible to escape but not impossible to overcome.  Yesterday was a result of that. I overcame… and if I can, so can you.🫶🏾

This past week Grandma Hagan passed away peacefully. She loved her friends, her faith, her home and the Williston community, her animals, her husband (together they’re “a prize”), and above all her great big family. She watched every swim race—big or small. She made every Christmas growing up special, but the greatest gifts she gave us were her love and a big family. What a blessing for all of us to be together a few weeks ago to celebrate her 100th birthday. Thankful for my mom, aunts and uncles, and the caregivers who allowed her to live a full and comfortable life all these years in her home. Proud to share her name Kathleen, but I’ll always be her Katie Gen. ❤️☘️

Every December from 2005-2015 (age 8-18), I swam in the Tom Dolan Invitational/the NCAP Invitational. Some of my favorite memories of my early days in the sport come from that meet. 10 years later and I’m headed back to swim an event at the Katie Ledecky Invitational next week. @ncap_swim ❤️

The first few years attending that meet, I was amazed watching @katemziegler break some American Records (and thus getting to learn firsthand about 🇺🇸 distance swimming). Kate and @tom_dolan always showed such kindness. 🫶🏼 Can’t wait to race in Maryland again, see so many familiar faces & friends around the pool deck, and meet the next generation of swimmers coming up in our great sport 🥹 @usaswimming

Katie Ledecky, the most decorated U.S. female Olympian of all time and former @gostanford student-athlete, will return to the Farm to speak at Stanford’s 134th Commencement ceremony.

At Stanford, she worked in the Mind & Body Lab while helping build on the university’s legacy as one of the most competitive in collegiate sports. In the pool, coached by Greg Meehan, she set 11 U.S. records, won eight NCAA titles and broke 15 NCAA records – while she and her @stanfordwswim teammates captured back-to-back NCAA team championships and two Pac-12 Conference team championships. Ledecky, a 14-time Olympic medalist who graduated in 2020 with a major in psychology and minor in political science, will address #Stanford2025 and their guests at Stanford Stadium on June 15.

“Stanford has played such a pivotal role in my educational and athletic life, and I look forward to honoring the graduates of the Class of 2025 as they dive into the next phases of their lives.”

‘'OCUPAR ESPAÇOS INEXPLORADOS E DESAFIAR ESTIGMAS’'

A skatista e empresária Letícia Bufoni conta, em sua coluna para o InfoMoney, como sua trajetória vai muito além das medalhas e dos títulos conquistados ao longo da carreira. 

Reconhecida mundialmente por sua excelência esportiva e por quebrar barreiras em esportes historicamente dominados por homens, Bufoni compartilha as experiências que a levaram a questionar o significado tradicional de sucesso e a colocar foco na representação e na criação de oportunidades para outras mulheres.

Bufoni fala não apenas seus feitos nas pistas, como recordes nos X-Games, mas também sua transição para o automobilismo feminino, atividades empreendedoras e escolhas ousadas de posicionamento de marca, como a parceria com o OnlyFans, que usa para compartilhar viagens, treinos e momentos em família.

Ao destacar a importância de ocupar espaços inexplorados e desafiar estigmas, a autora ressalta que o verdadeiro impacto de uma carreira esportiva reside na capacidade de inspirar, transformar narrativas e abrir portas para quem vem depois.

TEM BRASILEIRA NA WORLD SKATE! 🇧🇷🛹

Letícia Bufoni segue fazendo história e abrindo caminho para as mulheres no skate. A paulista foi anunciada como chefe da Comissão Técnica e agora integra o Conselho Executivo da federação internacional.

Bufoni terá participação na definição de aspectos operacionais do esporte, como formatos de competição, atribuição de pontos e classificações. Além disso, sua posição garante direito pleno a voto na Diretoria Executiva, da qual passa a ser membro.

Parabéns, @leticiabufoni! 👏

#TimeBrasil

World Skate are delighted to announce the appointment of Brazilian skateboarding superstar Letícia Bufoni to the Executive Board as Chair of the Skateboarding Technical Commission.

The most successful female skateboarder of all time, Letícia is one of the highest-profile skaters in the world.

As someone who has done more than most to change the perception of what women are capable of both within and without skateboarding, Letícia has inspired many young people around the globe to begin skateboarding in the first place.

Five-time X Games gold medallist, Tokyo Olympian, Guinness Book of World Records-holder, youth mentor; Letícia was a natural choice for appointment to the role by World Skate President Sabatino Aracu.

Leticia’s role as Chair of the Skateboarding Technical Commission will be both to advise on operational aspects of the World Skateboarding Tour such as contest formats, point allocations and rankings- as well as representing the views and ideas of the five continental Chairpeople who do likewise for their regions. The role carries full voting rights within our Executive Board, of which she becomes a member.

We spoke with Leticia on the advent of her announcement to give everyone a sense of
what she will bring to her new role.

Although we did not achieve the results we wanted at Nationals, we have so much to be proud of. Proud of the person we’ve become through this journey. Proud of our fight, resilience, and courage to face our fears. Proud of my team and what we’re building together. But most importantly, proud to be committed and faithful to the purpose and calling God has for my life.

Not every win comes with hardware. Sometimes the victory is just showing up when it’s hard. If you’re struggling or you’ve lost your hope, dig deep within and stay persistent. Know that the storms we face are temporary - and that there are always great treasures to be found in the end. Push further and strive to give it your all. I’m with and for you and believing your very best is still ahead ✨🙏🏾

As always, thank you for your love. I’m deeply humbled and touched by the warmth and prayers received by each and every one of you. It’s what has sustained us and continues to light the way forward. Our story isn’t finished. We’ll keep showing up and leaving space for God to show us just how good it can be.

UCLA Awards 💙 Thank you to @uclaalumni for this special honor as Young Alumnus of the Year. This place became a major turning point in my life. As a small town gal from Northern Michigan, I often felt like the foreigner, the other, the forgotten one. I came to UCLA in search of an identity outside of these labels, something I could craft that was entirely my own. 

What I found was a sense of belonging, a passion for lifting up marginalized voices and experiences and a purpose to build a more accessible and inclusive world.

College me could’ve never imagined the plans God had for my future. I marvel at his goodness and faithfulness then and all that he’s done since. Ask BIG things of God and watch him do more than you could ever pray for or dream of. He is able.

Bubba Wallace was running up front at the Cook Out 400 at Richmond, leading 123 laps and taking Stage 2, when a lug nut issue caused his left-front wheel to come off during a green-flag pit stop. The tire came off in the middle of pit lane, costing him multiple positions as he sat stopped. Joe Gibbs Racing’s No. 19 pit crew noticed what happened and stepped in to help 23XI Racing’s No. 23 team get the wheel back on so Wallace could continue. He eventually finished 31st, but the moment showed a rare level of respect between teams in the middle of a race.

When the mentals are in check.. it’s surreal how good life can be.

Doing it with your best friend is what life is all about. 

Thriving.

Yesterday my Olympic dream did not finish the way I dreamt it would. It wasn’t a story book ending or a fairy tail, it was just life. I dared to dream and had worked so hard to achieve it. Because in Downhill ski racing the difference between a strategic line and a catastrophic injury can be as small as 5 inches. 

I was simply 5 inches too tight on my line when my right arm hooked inside of the gate, twisting me and resulted in my crash. My ACL and past injuries had nothing to do with my crash whatsoever. 

Unfortunately, I sustained a complex tibia fracture that is currently stable but will require multiple surgeries to fix properly. 

While yesterday did not end the way I had hoped, and despite the intense physical pain it caused, I have no regrets. Standing in the starting gate yesterday was an incredible feeling that I will never forget. Knowing I stood there having a chance to win was a victory in and of itself. I also knew that racing was a risk. It always was and always will be an incredibly dangerous sport. 

And similar to ski racing, we take risks in life. We dream. We love. We jump. And sometimes we fall. Sometimes our hearts are broken. Sometimes we don’t achieve the dreams we know we could have. But that is the also the beauty of life; we can try. 

I tried. I dreamt. I jumped. 

I hope if you take away anything from my journey it’s that you all have the courage to dare greatly. Life is too short not to take chances on yourself. Because the only failure in life is not trying. 

I believe in you, just as you believed in me. 

❤️LV

Tomorrow: One last Olympic downhill run…

Just getting to these Olympics has been a journey, and one that some did not believe in from the start. I retired for 6 years, and because of a partial knee replacement, I had the chance to compete one more time. 

But why? Everyone seems to be asking me that question. But I think the answer is simple… I just love ski racing.

I am not unsure about life outside of sport. I am not searching for meaning or for attention or money. I know exactly who I am and I know exactly what I am made of. I am the product of amazing parents who showed me that hard work and determination pays off. My Mother, who is watching over me, taught me the power of positivity and resilience. My Father, who will be watching in the stands with my family and friends, taught me hard work and mental toughness.

I will stand in the starting gate tomorrow and know I am strong. Know that I believe in myself. Know that the odds are stacked against me with my age, no ACL, and a titanium knee- but know that I still believe.  And usually, when the odds are stacked against me the most, I pull the best of what’s inside me out. 

I will race tomorrow in my final Olympic Downhill and while I can’t guarantee a good result, I can guarantee I will give it everything I have. But no matter what happens, I have already won.

The outpouring of love and support over the past few days has been overwhelming in the best way. It has given me energy and helped me more than I can describe. Thank you 🙏🏻 

I believe💪🏻

Well… I completely tore my ACL last Friday. I also sustained a bone bruise (which is a common injury when you tear your ACL), plus meniscal tears but it’s unclear how much of that was there previously and what was new from the crash. 

This was obviously incredibly hard news to receive one week before the Olympics. I really appreciate everyone giving me time and space to process what happened and find a way forward. 

After extensive consultations with doctors, intense therapy, physical tests as well as skiing today, I have determined I am capable of competing in the Olympic Downhill on Sunday. Of course I will still need to do one training run, as is required to race on Sunday, but… I am confident in my body’s ability to perform. Despite my injuries my knee is stable, I do not have swelling and my muscles are firing and reacting as they should. I will obviously be continuing to evaluate with my medical team on a daily basis to make sure we are making smart decisions but I have every intention of competing on Sunday. 

I know what my chances in these Olympics were before this crash, and even though my chances aren’t the same now, there is still a chance. And as long as I have a chance, I will not lose hope. I will not give up! It’s not over yet! 

Thank you to everyone who has reached out and supported me. I feel the love and it is giving me strength. 🙏🏻💪🏻🇺🇸 

❤️ lindsey

When the ski world started whispering that 3-time Olympic medalist, Lindsey Vonn, must be missing something to stage a comeback after 6 years in retirement, Vonn had to set the record straight. “It’s actually really the opposite,” she says. “I’m missing a lot by coming back to ski racing.” So why is she putting her life on hold for the Milano-Cortina Games? Because the partial knee replacement that was meant to give her a pain-free life—the ability to walk her dogs, play tennis, and surf again, was so successful that it gave her permission to dream about one last Olympic run. But I have to thank all the haters for giving me extra motivation to keep pushing myself and fueling me when I was low. It feels good to know that after everything I have been through, I can still reach for the stars and grab them. Even at 41 years old. 

Never stop believing in yourself. Never stop dreaming. Never stop daring to do what everyone thinks you can’t. It’s only impossible until you do it!

MOM, I’M ON THE COVER OF TIME MAGAZINE!!!

As my eyes fill with tears (not ideal while doing intervals on the bike 🥹), I can’t quite put into words what this means to me. @TIME was always one of my mom’s favorite magazines. I can still see her in bed in Minnesota, reading each issue intently—ice cream in hand. I know she would be proud.

I never could have imagined, even in my wildest dreams, that my life would lead me here. I’m just a girl from Minnesota who wanted to ski fast. But this cover means I’ve done a lot more in my life than just ski fast. People might not know what I’ve done on the mountain, but they know that no matter how many times I fall, I will always pick myself back up, and I hope it inspires others to do the same!

At 41, I’m still chasing dreams, still pushing limits, still believing in what’s possible. My hope is that anyone reading this remembers: never give up on yourself. Never stop dreaming. ❤️

No matter what happens next, I’ve already won—because I’ve followed my heart, my passion, and my purpose. 🙏🏻

Thank you @jessicasibley @sampjacobs @ekelliher and @sgregory31 for helping make this moment a reality.

It’s World Mental Health Day… and I’ve been doing a lot of reflecting.

No one truly knows what someone else is going through. We often struggle in silence, putting on a brave face and pretending everything is fine — even when it’s not.

That’s why it’s so important to check in with the people you care about. Ask the questions that matter: “How are you really feeling?” Sometimes just knowing that someone cares — that someone truly wants to listen — can make all the difference.

I go through things every day that most people will never know about. But when I’m surrounded by friends, family, and teammates who care, it makes life lighter. Even when they don’t know exactly what I’m dealing with, their support means more than I could ever express.

And through it all, I’ve learned how important it is to hold on to the things that bring you joy. For me, skiing has always been one of those things — a place where I feel free, present, and connected to myself. It reminds me that even in the hardest moments, there’s beauty to be found in doing what you love.

Today is a reminder to check in with yourself and with others. Be kind. Reach out. Do the things that make you feel alive. You never know whose life — including your own — it might change. ❤️

I’m proud to be part of a vision that’s not just about buildings, but about belonging — a place where people from every neighborhood feel seen, connected, and inspired.”

The district is envisioned as a dynamic hub, seamlessly integrating retail, dining, public spaces, and the new stadium. Located on the former Producers Co-Op site just north of the Oklahoma River, it is uniquely positioned to unite Oklahoma City’s most vibrant destinations — Bricktown, the OKANA Resort, the Boathouse District, and Scissortail Park — transforming a historically underutilized site into a seamless, walkable neighborhood that stitches the city together through commerce, sports, culture and community.

Aquí os dejo un resumen del proceso de creación coreográfica junto a Marie-France Dubreuil para Madison Chock y Evan Bates, tricampeones del mundo y actuales referentes de la danza sobre hielo, representando a EE. UU.

Este es su programa definitivo, que presentarán en todas las competiciones de la temporada 2025–2026, incluidos los Juegos Olímpicos de Invierno de Milán 2026.

Un privilegio acompañar este proceso desde el estudio al hielo, y un enorme orgullo introducir la danza española en un programa tan relevante para nuestro deporte.

Gracias de corazón a Madison, Evan y al equipo de Ice Academy of Montreal por su confianza, cariño y generosidad.

A glimpse into the choreographic process with Marie-France Dubreuil for Madison Chock and Evan Bates — three-time World Champions and the top ice dance team in the world, representing the USA.

This is their definitive program, to be performed throughout the 2025–2026 season, including the Winter Olympic Games in Milan 2026.

It’s been an honor to shape this journey from studio to ice — and a true source of pride to bring Spanish dance into such a meaningful program for our sport.

Deepest thanks to Madison, Evan, and the Ice Academy of Montreal for their trust, warmth, and generosity.

Three years ago today, I underwent surgery—only to learn a few weeks later that it was stage 1 ovarian cancer.
Because it was caught early, I’m here—healthy, skating, and filled with gratitude.

Early detection saved my life, and it’s why continuing to work with Princess Margaret Cancer Centre and The Princess Margaret Cancer Foundation means so much to me. Helping spread awareness and encouraging people to listen to their bodies is something I hold very close to my heart.
I’m also deeply inspired by the recent $50 million donation to the Princess Margaret Foundation, dedicated to advancing early detection. The impact this will have on so many lives is truly incredible.

Please take care of yourselves. 💛 Getting checked can make all the difference.

After 62 long days in the NICU, we are finally bringing our baby boy home. Nolan was born 10 weeks early on November 16th at just 3 pounds 7 ounces. In his first 2 months Nolan has overcome chest tubes in both lungs due to holes in his lungs. Today he is leaving healthy as can be, one week before his original due date at 7 pounds 13 ounces! This journey has been one of the hardest and scariest things we have ever had to go through but it showed us how strong and resilient our son is. All the nurses kept telling us how feisty he is so we called him our “feisty fighter”. A huge thank you to the NICU nurses and doctors at @wolfsonchildren downtown Jacksonville. NICU nurses are literal angels on this earth and we can’t thank you enough for taking care of our son for two months and keeping him alive! We truly couldn’t be happier to finally have him home. 
God is so good!! 
Isaiah 41:10 “So do not fear, for I am with you; I will strengthen you and help you; I will uphold you with my righteous hand.”
